两个周年纪念日。

两年前的今天，随着卢沟桥的枪声，那场“事变”开始了。这场事变完全违背了发起者的意愿，已演变为两个民族之间极其严重和重大的冲突。无论是一年前还是今天，我们都看不到这场官方未宣战的战争的尽头；在世界任何其他地方都不像在远东那样，更不宜进行预言。只有一件事是确定的，即我们正经历一个涉及远东关系发生巨大变化的阶段，而且在这场斗争之后，无论谁赢得战争（如果真有胜利者的话），欧洲列强以及美国都将面临一个全新的局面。

在此背景下，让我们回顾今天的另一个周年纪念日。一百年前的今天，即1839年7月7日，一名中国人在广州与一名英国水手的争吵中被杀。很难说这一事件是否是必要的，因为它使自那年年初以来因鸦片问题而已经紧张的中英关系公开化；无论如何，它确实影响了那位精力充沛的满洲特使林则徐。林则徐是皇帝因鸦片纠纷专门从北京派往广州的，他采取了针对英国人的行动。在广州处于危急境地的英国人做出了让步，同意将其拥有的共计20,283箱鸦片交给中国人销毁，并于5月24日撤离至澳门。此后，他们本将被迫完全离开中国水域，但当明显看出继续一般贸易（除鸦片贸易外）对中国人极为有利和有益时，他们返回广州就变得可取了。

恰如一年前一样，尽管日本人制造了许多新的局势，但今天同样重要的是，没有人能确切地说出远东目前的状况如何。一年前的预言已成现实：即使在汉口失守后，战争仍以不减的韧性继续进行，今天无人怀疑，即使重庆陷落也不会看到战争的结束。诚然，凡日军为军事行动做好准备的地方，他们都取得了一些具有军事重要性的成果，考虑到他们通往当今前线的交通线规模巨大，这一点在组织方面或许更为明显。占领广州、在海南岛登陆、占领西沙群岛和北海附近的涠洲岛、过去几周沿中国海岸的行动、占领汕头和其他据点，并未对总体战局产生本质改变，尽管这些成功改善了日本相对于外国列强的战略地位。蒋介石的中国正缓慢但稳步地向内陆和西部的广阔空间发展，

pages.en:
- 3 -
expression of which development is being found in the fact
that during the last few years a new province named Hsikang,
west of Szechuen, came into being.
Still more decisive than the preservation of the
economic and military power of resistance, is the fact that
the National Government has succeeded from preserving herself
from decomposition as a result of inner forces. Wang Ching
Wei's attempts, in his own way and independently of the
Generalissimo, or perhaps by bringing pressure to bear on
the latter, to bring about the peace either by becoming a
middleman between Chungking and Tokyo or as a leader in the
Japanese occupied territory, have completely failed. It
remains yet to be seen in what manner his endeavours, which
people acquainted with the situation do not consider as being
entirely treacherous, were obstructed by the Japanese themselves,
or to what degree he lacked the Chinese support, at any rate
one thing is certain: Chiang Kai Shek's authority remains un-
shaken, his word alone decides on war or peace. A few weeks
ago when China was passing through the darkest hours of her
existence, his government completely broke off relations with
Wang Ching Wei. If our information is correct, Wang Ching
Wei is pursuing his endeavours. That he has failed in winning
over Marshal Wu Pei Fu for his plans, appears to be certain.
But it is also likely that the Japanese, considering the im-
possibility of making any real progress in the occupied Chinese
territory, are seeking new ways to bring about an improvement.
To what degree Japan has been weakened by the war
is difficult to say to-day; available estimates and opinions
appear to be onesided. It is certain that the New Order can-
not be established by the military alone, and it is equally
certain that it cannot be realized in a country harassed by
guerilla activities and without the authority of a proper
Chinese Government - be it in Peiping, Nanking or Canton.

- 3 -
这种发展的一个表现是，在过去几年里，四川西部出现了一个名为西康的新省份。
比保持经济和军事抵抗力量更为决定性的事实是，国民政府成功地避免了因内部力量而瓦解。汪精卫试图以自己的方式，独立于委员长之外，或者 perhaps 通过对后者施加压力，要么作为重庆和东京之间的中间人，要么作为日本占领区的领导人来促成和平，但这些尝试已彻底失败。仍有待观察的是，他的努力——熟悉局势的人并不认为这些努力完全是背叛行为——在多大程度上被日本人自己所阻碍，或者他在多大程度上缺乏中国人的支持；无论如何，有一点是肯定的：蒋介石的权威依然不可动摇，只有他的话才能决定战争或和平。几周前，当中国处于其存在的最黑暗时刻时，他的政府完全断绝了与汪精卫的关系。如果我们的情报准确，汪精卫仍在追求他的目标。他未能争取吴佩孚元帅加入其计划，这似乎是肯定的。但也很可能，鉴于在被占领的中国领土上无法取得任何真正进展，日本人正在寻求新的途径以带来改善。
日本因战争而被削弱的程度今天难以言说；现有的估计和意见似乎都有片面性。可以肯定的是，“新秩序”不能仅靠军事手段建立，同样肯定的是，在一个受游击活动困扰且没有适当中国政府（无论是在北平、南京还是广州）权威的国家中，它是无法实现的。

In connection with all these questions emerges the
problem brought up by Japan, of the International Settlements,
foreign concessions and therewith connected position of the
European powers and America in the Far East. All this,
however, is still in the air; the blockade of Tientsin goes
on and has become practically a habit while the Anglo-Japanese
conversations at Tokyo have not yet begun.

The political developments in the Far East have become
still closer bound to the political situation in Europe than
was the case last year. The feeling of general insecurity is
more distinct than before. One may say that at the commence-
ment of the 3rd year of war in China, the outlook does not
appear hopeful to anyone, but least of all to the foreign
businessman.

It is most remarkable that precisely to-day, hundred
years after the beginning of the economical development of
the China coast, much less attention is being paid to the
interests of merchants than was the case in 1839 by the forces
at hand, which bring other important factors to the foreground.

In the carrying out of her economic development and
military resistance, China welcomes financial and technical
support of friendly powers. Dr. Sun Yat Sen's principles of
the world political development of China will always remain
China's guiding principles in her national reconstruction. If
China appreciates the help given her in war time, she will also
co-operate with the foreign powers in the execution of greater
problems which await her after the conclusion of the war.
The foreign powers should take heed of the Japanese policy of
aggression.

Dr. Wang Chung-hui informed the powers who want to
preserve the equilibrium in the Pacific that they can do so
in no other way than by breaking up all economic connections
with Japan. China will continue to offer resistance, which

与所有这些问题相关的是，日本提出的关于国际租界、外国租界以及由此涉及的欧洲列强和美国在远东地位的问题。然而，这一切仍悬而未决；天津的封锁仍在继续，并几乎成为一种常态，而英日在东京的会谈尚未开始。

远东的政治发展与欧洲政治局势的联系比去年更加紧密。普遍的不安全感比以前更为明显。可以说，在中国战争进入第三年之际，前景对任何人来说都显得不乐观，对外国商人来说尤其如此。

最引人注目的是，恰恰在今天，即中国沿海经济发展开始的一百年后，人们对商人利益的关注远少于1839年，因为当时的现有力量将其他重要因素推到了前台。

在进行经济发展和军事抵抗的过程中，中国欢迎友好国家的财政和技术支持。孙中山博士关于中国世界政治发展的原则将始终是中国国家重建的指导原则。如果中国感激战时给予她的帮助，她也将与外国列强合作，执行战后等待她的更大问题。外国列强应警惕日本的侵略政策。

王宠惠博士告知那些希望维持太平洋平衡的列强，他们只有通过切断与日本的所有经济联系才能做到这一点。中国将继续进行抵抗，这种

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,
JUL 8 1939

Anniversary Passes
Shanghai's garrison and internal security
forces yesterday were mobilized on the occa-
sion of July 7, the second anniversary of the
outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities at
the Marco Polo Bridge, and at the time of
writing nothing unusual had occurred. Based
on a very efficient and comprehensive scheme
the International Settlement and the French
Concession were virtually divided into two
separate areas, and passage from one to the
other was possible only through streets where
pedestrians and cars were subjected to search
to prevent the infiltration or movement of
terrorists. Lord Elibank's fear that the Japanese
might act against the foreign areas did not
materialize. Rather, there were co-operative
measures in the foreign areas and Japanese-
controlled areas to prevent any disturbances
which might interfere with the peace and good
order of Shanghai, and as the population is ac-
customing itself to these precautionary mobiliz-
ations only a minimum of interference was
caused as Shanghai's international guards per-
formed their duties. By midnight there was a
relaxation of measures although the extreme
necessity for vigilance was not ignored. The
manner in which the foreign authorities have
been able to mobilize against eventualities is
a tribute to the careful planning and organiza-
tion by those responsible, and the co-operation
of volunteers in both areas to make the plan
successful. The French "Specials" took over
police duties in the Concession on Thursday
night and last night, and the International
Settlement Volunteers and "Specials" also did
their bit with the regular police and military
forces. These emergencies based more on ap-
prehension than fact are unfortunate and de-
mand the strictest attention, but, as yesterday's
mobilization demonstrated, the community by
its voluntary service stands solidly behind the
authorities in the desire that the essential con-
ditions of peace and order be maintained, and
whatever are the political difficulties engend-
ered by conditions Shanghai's neutrality shall
be scrupulously observed.

1939年7月8日

周年纪念日过去
昨天，正值7月7日——卢沟桥中日敌对行动爆发两周年纪念日，上海驻军和内部安全部队进行了动员，截至发稿时，未发生任何异常情况。基于一个非常高效和全面的方案，公共租界和法租界实际上被划分为两个独立的区域，从一个区域到另一个区域只能通过街道通行，行人和车辆在这些街道上接受搜查，以防止恐怖分子的渗透或移动。埃利班克勋爵（Lord Elibank）担心日本人可能会对外国区域采取行动的担忧并未成为现实。相反，在外国区域和日本控制区采取了合作措施，以防止任何可能干扰上海和平与良好秩序的骚乱，由于民众已习惯于这些预防性动员，因此造成的干扰最小，上海的国际警卫人员在履行职责。午夜时分，措施有所放松，尽管极度警惕的必要性并未被忽视。外国当局能够针对突发事件进行动员的方式，是对负责人员精心计划和组织的赞誉，也是两个区域的志愿者合作使计划成功的证明。法国“特别警察”在周四晚上和昨晚接管了租界的警务工作，公共租界义勇队和“特别警察”也与正规警察和军事部队一起尽了力。这些更多基于担忧而非事实的紧急情况是不幸的，需要最严格的关注，但是，正如昨天的动员所展示的那样，社区通过其志愿服务坚定地支持当局，希望维持和平与秩序的基本条件，并且无论局势引发何种政治困难，上海的中立地位都将得到严格遵守。

卷宗
B 8/7

JUL 3 1939

Chinese Inactive
On Anniversary
No Meetings Held or Flags
Flown in Foreign Areas; One
Minute Silence Suggested

Silence was the keynote of the
commemoration of the second anni-
versary of the July 7 Incident by the
Chinese in Shanghai yesterday, no
meetings being held. As a contrast
against the conditions existing on the
first anniversary of the same incident
from which the present large-scale
Sino-Japanese hostilities were started,
there was no Chinese flag display
and there was a noticeable absence
of anti-Japanese propaganda and
publicity, probably owing to the
rigid press control effected by Settle-
ment authorities.
Last year, the Shanghai office of
the Kuomintang was still able to issue
orders to the Chinese here telling them
of the various methods of commemo-
rating the day but the Chinese press
yesterday did not publish this order.
Only one report stated that the Chi-
nese here should turn vegetarians on
the day and observe one-minute's
silence at noon in honour of the dead.
Commenting on the anniversary the
"Shun Pao" stated that the anniver-
sary is not "epoch-making" inasmuch
as both sides to the dispute would not
give in. After fighting for two years
no peace is in sight. The Japanese
have been unable to end the hostilities
quickly as they wished, while the Chi-
nese have started to attack the rear
of Japanese forces. There are three
possibilities of creating "peace-making
events," namely, suspension of hos-
tilities by the Japanese, general coun-
ter offensive by the Chinese and
mediation by the Powers. It is point-
ed out, however, that so far the latter
have not taken action to cause the
suspension of hostilities. The paper
opines therefore that the second an-
niversary is merely a time counter.
Apart from broadcasting a speech
on Thursday night, Mayor Fu Hsiao-
en of Greater Shanghai issued a state-
ment through the "Sin Shun Pao"
yesterday commemorating the anni-
versary. In this statement he blamed
the Communists and General Chiang
Kai-shek for the hostilities. He urged
people to refuse to co-operate with
General Chiang and to cultivate
friendship with Japan so that the two
countries may jointly carry out the
"new order" in the East Asia.

1939年7月3日

中国人在纪念日保持静默
外侨区域未举行集会或悬挂旗帜；建议默哀一分钟

昨日，上海中国人在纪念“七七事变”两周年时，以静默为主基调，未举行任何集会。与一年前该事件（即当前大规模中日敌对行动之起点）周年纪念时的状况形成对比的是，此次没有展示中国国旗，反日宣传和公开活动也明显缺席，这可能是因为租界当局实施了严格的新闻管制。
去年，国民党上海办事处仍能向在沪华人发布命令，告知纪念该日的各种方式，但昨日的中文报纸并未刊登此命令。仅有一则报道指出，在沪华人应在当日素食，并于正午时分默哀一分钟，以悼念死者。
《申报》在评论该周年纪念日时称，鉴于争端双方均不让步，该纪念日并非“划时代”的事件。经过两年的战斗，和平仍无望。日本人未能如他们所愿迅速结束敌对行动，而中国人已开始攻击日军后方。制造“促和事件”有三种可能性，即：日本停止敌对行动、中国发动全面反攻以及列强调停。然而，文章指出，迄今为止，列强尚未采取行动促使停止敌对行动。因此，该报认为，两周年纪念日仅仅是一个时间计数器。
除了周四晚间广播演讲外，大上海市长傅筱庵昨日通过《新申报》发表声明，纪念该周年。在该声明中，他将敌对行动归咎于共产党人和蒋介石将军。他敦促民众拒绝与蒋介石将军合作，并与日本培养友谊，以便两国共同在东亚实施“新秩序”。

JUL 8 1939

War Anniversary
Passes Quietly
No Incidents Occur
As Police, Military
Watch Over City

With the exception of a few anti-Japanese slogans which had been chalked on walls in the Pootoo Road and Gordon Road districts overnight and a few pamphlets that were distributed in various throughfares of the western district, yesterday's second anniversary of the commencement of hostilities in North-China passed quietly and saw a marked reduction in crime as underworld characters did not deem it advisable to venture forth into the city's streets where armed patrols were on duty from 5 a.m. until early this morning. The exemplary manner in which the Settlement and the Concession were patrolled once again demonstrated to Shanghai's population that the authorities concerned are in a position to cope with any eventuality.

With the exception of Armoured Car Co., and the Russian Regiment, S. V. C., members of the Shanghai Volunteer Corps, whilst attending their various offices in uniform, did not patrol the streets until after 5 p.m. as did the Police Specials who engaged in searches in the Louza and Sinza districts.

All Chinese amusement resorts were ordered closed by the police yesterday, whilst roof-gardens were not permitted to remain open, as an added precautionary measure.

As far as could be ascertained late last night, no arrests or seizures were made either in the Settlement or in the Concession, where similar measures had been in force since early yesterday morning.

Japanese Naval launches were in evidence on the Whangpoo throughout the morning, carefully scrutinizing all river traffic but no untoward incident was reported from there.

The precautionary measures enforced in both foreign districts, remained unchanged with a few exceptions from those first put in force on August 13, of last year. The French Police however forced all owners of buildings facing Avenue Edward VII, to lock their doors unto that throughfare as an added measure of precaution whilst the British military were on duty on the Chapoo and Szechuen Road bridges in addition to Garden Bridge.

By a late hour last night however, all precautionary measures were cancelled and it was anticipated that most of the barbed wire barricades would be removed from the city's streets before this morning, much to the relief of drivers and bus users, some of the latter having been considerably inconvenienced due to the deviation of certain routes on account of the barricades.

1939年7月8日

战争周年平静度过
警察与军队监视城市，未发生事件

除了普陀路和戈登路地区夜间墙上被粉笔写上的几条反日标语，以及西区各主要街道散发的几份传单外，昨日华北战事爆发两周年纪念日平静度过，犯罪率显著下降，因为黑社会人物认为不宜冒险走上街头，那里从凌晨5点至今晨早些时候一直有武装巡逻队执勤。公共租界和法租界的巡逻方式堪称典范，再次向上海市民表明，有关当局有能力应对任何突发事件。

除装甲车连和俄国团外，上海万国商团（S. V. C.）成员身着制服前往各自办公地点，但直到下午5点后才像警察特别队（Police Specials）那样在街上巡逻，后者在老闸和新闸地区进行了搜查。

昨日，警方下令所有中式娱乐场所关闭，作为额外的预防措施，屋顶花园也不允许开放。

截至昨晚深夜查明，公共租界和法租界均未发生逮捕或没收行动，法租界自昨日清晨起也实施了类似措施。

整个上午，黄浦江上可见日本海军汽艇，仔细检查所有江面交通，但未报告发生任何不幸事件。

两个外侨区域实施的预防措施，除少数例外情况外，与去年8月13日首次实施的措施保持不变。然而，法国警察强迫所有面向爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）的建筑物业主锁闭朝向该干道的门户，作为额外的预防措施；同时，英军除了在外白渡桥执勤外，还在乍浦路和四川路桥上执勤。

然而，到昨晚深夜，所有预防措施均已取消，预计大部分铁丝网路障将在今天上午之前从城市街道上移除，这让司机和公交车乘客松了一口气，其中一些乘客因路障导致某些路线改道而深感不便。

Japanese Observances
With simplicity as the dominating
note, local Japanese yesterday ob-
served the second anniversary of the
outbreak of the Sino-Japanese con-
flict. The principal function was the
service at the Shanghai Shrine, where
residents gathered at 11 o'clock in
the morning to observe a one-minute
silence for the war dead.
Japanese schools, factories, banks,
business firms and other civilian or-
ganizations held individual assemblies
of their staffs to listen to a reading
of the Imperial Rescript granted on
the occasion of the first anniversary
of the conflict. The articles of the
National Spiritual Mobilization move-
ment were recited by those present.
One-course meals were served at
restaurants and in homes, while a tag
campaign was conducted on the
streets of Hongkew and Yangtsepoo
by members of the Shanghai Japan-
ese Women's Emergency Committee.
Contributions to the National De-
fence Fund were also sought of their
staffs by various Japanese organiza-
tions. Empty bottles and cans, scrap
iron, tin foil, old blankets, discarded
clothing, newspapers and magazines
were collected at various Japanese
schools to be sent to Japan for re-
processing.
Major Tsuneo Yano, staff officer of
the Japanese Army Shanghai Defence
Force headquarters, broadcast an
address over the radio at 7 o'clock
Friday evening.

1984

日本人的纪念活动
昨日，在沪日本人以简朴为主基调，纪念中日冲突爆发两周年。主要活动是在上海神社举行的仪式，居民于上午11点聚集，为战争死者默哀一分钟。
日本的学校、工厂、银行、商行和其他民间组织分别举行了员工集会，聆听宣读在冲突一周年之际颁布的《帝国诏书》。在场人员诵读了《国民精神总动员运动纲领》。
餐馆和家庭提供单道菜餐食，上海日本妇女紧急委员会成员在虹口和杨浦的街道上开展了佩戴徽章募捐活动。
各日本机构也向其员工募集国防基金捐款。各日本学校收集空瓶和罐头、废铁、锡箔、旧毯子、废弃衣物、报纸和杂志，运往日本进行再加工。
日本陆军上海防卫队司令部参谋矢野恒雄少佐于周五晚上7点通过无线电广播发表了讲话。

pages.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
JUL 7 1939

Anniversary Precautions
Shanghai Police and Defence Forces Stand
By for Emergency, No Incident Expected

TO the casual observer, Shanghai last night on the eve of
the second anniversary of the outbreak of the war in North-
China presented the same carefree appearance that is its usual
front. Crowds on the "gay white way" of Nanking Road and
other down-town night haunts moved slowly up and down the
streets in lazy waves of humanity. Behind the scenes, however,
in every police station in the International Settlement, Specials
of the Shanghai Municipal Police stood by in full kit, ready to
move on the job at a second's notice.
These Specials stood by until the
curfew hour last night. In addition
to the Specials, the Reserve Unit
also was held in readiness. In anti-
cipation of a large number of arrests
the S.M.P. commandeered the old
Amoy Road gaol, previously used by
the Salvation Army, to lodge the
expected overflow of suspicious
characters. One entire floor of cells
was cleared out in readiness for
prospective tenants. Across the
creek, in the North Kiangse Road
and North Shanse Road district,
Japanese Consular Police co-operat-
ed with members of the Shanghai
Municipal Police in carrying out ex-
tensive searching operations. Hard-
working crews of men spent the
night erecting barbed wire barricades
in various parts of the Settlement
and French Concession.
Streets Barricaded
Many smaller thoroughfares have
been barricaded off so as to reduce
the number of policemen required
to maintain a close check on every-
thing that happens in the streets,
whilst British, American and Italian
troops were patrolling their respec-
tive sectors from a late hour last
night, and intensive search-opera-
tions by the police commenced earlier
yesterday evening. The Russian
Regiment, S.V.C., has been on duty
since last night and members of the
regiment are mostly posted at Settle-
ment inlets, where they second police
parties engaged in scrutinizing
vehicles and pedestrians.
With the exception of the Armour-
ed Car Co., S.V.C., which has been
mobilized from 5 a.m. today, the
other units of the Corps are on "pre-
cautionary," which means that volun-
teers and Police Specials will attend
their usual occupations in uniforms,
ready to be called out at a few
minutes notice. Towards the eve-
ning, they are likely to be used in
patrolling streets, if last year's effi-
cient precautions are taken as a pat-
tern, whilst the Police Riot Squad
will be on duty until late tonight.
Curfew will be strictly enforced
also in the French Concession. Persons
without curfew passes were closely
questioned last night by the Specials
who were on duty and who will
again relieve the regulars from night-
fall tonight, by taking over certain
duties particularly curfew enforce-
ment in all parts of the Concession.
The French troops are patrolling the
various streets and the light armoured
cars with mounted machine-guns
were also much in evidence last night.
In the Settlement, the Armoured
cars of the S.V.C., were patrolling
last night and military lorries with
Russian Regiment details, were seen
along Great Western Road and other
outlying thoroughfares.

《字林西报》，
1939年7月7日

周年纪念预防措施
上海警察和防卫部队待命应对紧急情况，预计不会发生事件

对于偶然的观察者来说，昨晚在华北战争爆发两周年前夕，上海呈现出其惯常的无忧无虑的面貌。南京路“欢乐白光大道”及其他市中心夜间娱乐场所的人群，像慵懒的人潮波浪一样在街道上缓慢来回移动。然而，在幕后，在国际租界的每个警察局，上海公共租界工部局警务处的特别队员全副武装待命，准备随时出动执行任务。
这些特别队员一直待命至昨晚宵禁时间。除特别队员外，后备队也处于待命状态。鉴于预期会有大量逮捕行动，上海公共租界工部局警务处征用了旧的厦门路监狱（此前由救世军使用），以收容预期的可疑人员溢出部分。整整一层楼的牢房已被清空，以备 prospective tenants（预期入住者）。在苏州河对岸，北江西路和北山西路地区，日本领事警察与上海公共租界工部局警务处成员合作，进行了大规模的搜查行动。辛勤工作的人员整夜在公共租界和法租界的各个部分架设铁丝网路障。
街道设置路障
许多较小的干道已被路障封锁，以减少维持对街道上发生的一切进行严密监控所需的警察人数，而英国、美国和意大利军队从昨晚深夜开始在其各自防区巡逻，警方的密集搜查行动于昨日傍晚较早时开始。上海万国商团俄国团自昨晚起一直执勤，该团成员大多部署在公共租界入口处，协助警察小队检查车辆和行人。
除上海万国商团装甲车连已于今日凌晨5点动员外，该团其他单位处于“预防性”状态，这意味着志愿者和警察特别队员将身着制服从事日常职业，准备在几分钟通知内被召集。如果以去年的高效预防措施为范本，他们可能在傍晚被用于街道巡逻，而警察防暴队将执勤至今晚深夜。
法租界也将严格执行宵禁。昨晚，执勤的特别队员对没有宵禁通行证的人进行了严密盘问，他们将从今晚黄昏起再次接替正规警察，承担法租界各地特别是执行宵禁的特定职责。法国军队正在巡逻各条街道，昨晚还随处可见装有车载机枪的轻型装甲车。
在公共租界，上海万国商团的装甲车昨晚一直在巡逻，载有俄国团分队的军用卡车在大西路和其他外围干道上被发现。

pages.en:
No Incidents Expected
Police officials questioned yesterday, did not anticipate any untoward incident, although they were taking no chances and, whilst actual details of the precautionary measures were not divulged, it was understood that they were substantially the same as last year.
Traffic is bound to be slowed up from the restricted number of thoroughfares available but, as in the past, it is only reasonable to assume that persons thus inconvenienced will realize the necessity for these measures which are intended to maintain peace and order in the foreign area of Shanghai.
In Hongkew and other Japanese-occupied districts of the Settlement, extra-ordinary precautions have already been taken for a number of days, by the Japanese Naval Landing Party, patrols of which are actively engaged in searching pedestrians and houses.
Up to an early hour this morning, however, everything was quiet whilst the unusually large number of armed men on the streets may have indicated to some late homecomers that "something was in the air." All members of the Settlement and Concession police forces were confined to barracks last night, whilst members of the Shanghai Defence Forces, have also had their leaves cancelled. In all military barracks and police stations, a certain number of men are being kept in preparedness, fully armed, so that they may be dispatched to any trouble centre the moment an alarm is received.
The S.V.C. gymnasium has been converted into a dormitory for the Russian Regiment, whilst platoons are standing by at various concentration centres, with trucks ready to convey them to wherever they may be needed.
Wild rumours of trouble in Hongkew last night caused the Japanese authorities to bottle up the area across the creek about 9.45 p.m. Every bridge leading to Hongkew from the International Settlement was closed down simultaneously and all traffic prohibited from either entering or leaving the district North of the creek. Revellers in the night spots over the creek were caused considerable anxiety as this news spread from place to place. Several people residing in the Settlement feared that they would have to spend the night in Hongkew. At length, after being closed for 35 minutes, the bridges opened up again at 10.20 p.m. and traffic was resumed.
pages.zh:
预计不会发生事件
昨日接受询问的警察官员并未预料到会发生任何不幸事件，尽管他们并未掉以轻心，虽然预防措施的具体细节未予透露，但据悉这些措施与去年大体相同。
由于可用的干道数量有限，交通势必放缓，但正如过去一样，只有合理假设那些因此感到不便的人会认识到这些措施的必要性，其目的是维持上海外侨区域的和平与秩序。
在虹口及公共租界其他日本占领区，日本海军陆战队数日前已采取非凡的预防措施，其巡逻队积极从事搜查行人和房屋的工作。
然而，直到今天清晨早些时候，一切都很平静，尽管街道上异常大量的武装人员可能向一些晚归者暗示“气氛有些不对劲”。公共租界和法租界警察部队的所有成员昨晚都被限制在营房内，上海防卫部队的成员也被取消了休假。在所有军营和警察局，一定数量的人员保持全副武装的准备状态，以便一旦收到警报即可派遣至任何骚乱中心。
上海万国商团体育馆已被改建为俄国团的宿舍，而各排则在各个集结中心待命，卡车准备将他们运送至任何需要的地方。
昨晚关于虹口发生骚乱的荒谬谣言导致日本当局在晚上9点45分左右封锁了苏州河对岸的区域。连接国际租界与虹口的所有桥梁同时关闭，禁止所有交通进入或离开苏州河北部的地区。随着这一消息在各处传播，苏州河对岸夜总会的寻欢作乐者感到相当焦虑。几位居住在公共租界的人担心他们不得不在虹口过夜。最终，在关闭35分钟后，桥梁于晚上10点20分重新开放，交通恢复。

pages.en:
NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS,

JUL 7 1939

Quiet Wanted Today
With the authorities taking every precaution against any outbreak of disorders today, the second anniversary of the Lukuochiao incident, it is to be hoped that the day will pass off without trouble. It certainly will if those who might feel inclined to stir up disorder, by over-enthusiastic demonstration refrain from doing so, a remark which applies to them no matter what may happen to be their political opinions. The International Settlement and the French Concession afforded asylum to hundreds of thousands of refugees when hostilities broke out in this area; they are continuing to do so, though a large number of refugees have sought their old homes out in the environs of the city. All these people owe a debt of gratitude to the foreign areas which saved them from all the perils of war, and cared for the destitute in a manner which, considering all the circumstances, was nothing short of wonderful. It would indeed be a lasting reproach to them if they were now to take advantage of that neutrality which provided protection for them, and assisted in bringing about a state of affairs which would be as unfortunate to them as it would be to their fellow residents. Patriotism is not displayed by outbreaks of turbulence in circumstances such as prevail in Shanghai, indeed those guilty of such conduct behave in the most unpatriotic manner possible, as playing into the hands of those whom they regard as their enemies, and obviously no Chinese who is worth his salt would willingly indulge in such courses. The dispositions which authorities of the two foreign areas have made against possible eventualities appear sufficient to cope with any disorder which may arise, but the Chinese residents of Shanghai, no matter what their political opinions may be, can with justice be expected to cooperate with those authorities, as the best manner of emphasizing their convictions.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，

1939年7月7日

今日求静

鉴于当局正采取一切预防措施，以防在今日——卢沟桥事变两周年纪念日——发生任何骚乱，人们希望这一天能平安无事地度过。如果那些可能因过度热情的示威而倾向于煽动混乱的人克制自己，那么这一天肯定会平安无事；这一劝告适用于他们所有人，无论其政治观点如何。当战事在本地区爆发时，公共租界和法租界为数十万难民提供了庇护；尽管大量难民已前往城市周边的旧居，但租界仍在继续提供庇护。所有这些人都欠外国区域一份感激之情，因为这些区域使他们免受战争的所有危险，并在考虑到所有情况的前提下，以堪称奇妙的方式照顾贫困者。如果他们现在利用为他们提供保护的中立地位，协助造成一种对他们自己及其同胞居民同样不幸的事态，那确实将成为他们身上持久的污点。在上海目前 prevailing 的情况下，爱国精神并非通过爆发动荡来体现；事实上，犯下此类行为的人表现得极其不爱国，因为这正中他们所视为敌人者的下怀；显然，任何有骨气的中国人都不会自愿沉溺于此类行径。两个外国区域当局为应对可能发生的情况所做的部署，似乎足以应付可能出现的任何混乱；但上海的华人居民，无论其政治观点如何，都有理由被期望与这些当局合作，以此作为强调其信念的最佳方式。

pages.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

JUL 7 1939

AFTER TWO YEARS

Two years ago today, while Japanese forces
were engaged in "night manœuvres" in the
vicinity of Lukouchiao, some shots were
alleged to have been fired at them by Chinese
who afterwards disappeared. That was the
commencement of a war, which has been
euphemistically called the "China Incident."
It does not matter now what intentions the
Japanese had of confining the trouble to
North China, and it appears that at one time
they did intend so to localize it, the fact
remains that hostilities spread until rather
over a month later the environs of Shanghai
became involved, and this city had to pass
through a grimmer experience of fighting
than occurred on the previous occasion in
1932. Attempts have been made to criticize
the Chinese for attacking the Japanese at
Shanghai, but, once the China Incident had
commenced, they were entitled to strike at
their enemy wherever they found him, and
one such place was Shanghai. The im-
mediate effect of this development was to
commit the Japanese more deeply in China
than it is apparent they originally intended,
for it is believed that, had they remained
unmolested, their scheme envisaged taking
only that portion of China north of the old
bed of the Yellow River, and the establish-
ment in that area of a Government not un-
like in status that of Manchoukuo. That
scheme miscarried, and, under the plea of
eradicating Chiang Kai-shek and the Kuo-
mintang, the Japanese extended their opera-
tions until now, at the conclusion of two
years fighting, they are engaged the whole
length of the Chinese coastline and as far
into the interior as the Canton-Hankow and
the Peiping-Hankow Railway lines. All the
principal ports in China are in Japanese
hands, and while it would be incorrect to
suggest that they control the areas into which
they have penetrated, or that they will be
able to for a very long time to come, it is,
nevertheless, true that they have disrupted,
even if they have not succeeded in wiping
out the due processes of the Chinese Govern-
ment they are seeking to destroy. The
magnitude of the effort may be judged by
the latest reports that Japanese has now
about 40 divisions in the field in China, while
it has also been claimed that the Yangtze is
the channel for the supply of about one
million troops in Central China.

Thus, from what was at first believed
would be a comparatively local incident, in-
volving the use of a minimum of force, Japan
has become increasingly committed until the
forces she is using suggest that she is engaged
in a major war, which indeed she is. Of the
amount of money she has spent, and is spend-
ing, and the cost of this adventure to her
in the lives of her sons, there is no means
of ascertaining exact figures. The returns of
casualties suffered are under suspicion of be-
ing considerably minimized, but from various
statements which have been made by Japan-
ese leaders from time to time it may be as-
sumed that the cost in money is somewhere
in the neighbourhood of Yen 15,000,000,000,
of actual expenditure, with a loss in trade,
etc., which cannot easily be estimated. To
offset this it is necessary to consider her
gains. With the coastline completely under
Japanese control a stranglehold has been
placed upon Chinese trade, and the economic
life of the country has been dealt a serious
blow. It is true that some trade can be
carried on by means of the Burma route and
overland with Soviet Russia, and military sup-
plies can be secured by the same means, but
both channels have their disadvantages which
are particularly noticeable when need for
quick delivery is taken into consideration.
But that is all the Japanese have secured.
It is true that they are able to carry on a
certain amount of business up the Yangtze,
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。

1939年7月7日

两年之后

两年前的今天，当日军正在卢沟桥附近进行“夜间演习”时，据称有中国人向他们开枪，随后这些人消失无踪。那是一场战争的开端，这场战争被委婉地称为“中国事变”。日本当时是否有意将冲突限制在华北，以及他们是否曾一度打算如此局部化冲突，如今已不再重要；事实是，敌对行动不断蔓延，直到一个多月后，上海周边地区也被卷入，这座城市不得不经历比1932年上一次更为惨烈的战斗。有人试图批评中国人在上海攻击日本人，但是，一旦“中国事变”开始，他们就有权在任何发现敌人的地方打击敌人，而上海就是这样一个地方。这一发展的直接后果是，使日本在中国陷入的程度比其最初打算的更深；因为人们相信，如果不受干扰，他们的计划仅 envisaged 占领黄河故道以北的那部分中国领土，并在该地区建立一个地位类似于满洲国的政府。该计划失败了，在日本人以铲除蒋介石和国民党为借口的情况下，他们扩大了作战范围，直到如今，在两年的战斗结束时，他们的兵力遍布整个中国海岸线，并深入内陆至粤汉铁路和平汉铁路沿线。中国所有主要港口均在日本人手中；虽然暗示他们控制着已渗透的地区，或暗示他们在未来很长一段时间内能够控制这些地区，是不正确的，但不可否认的是，即使他们未能成功抹除他们寻求摧毁的中国政府的正常运作程序，他们也已经破坏了这些程序。从最新报告称日本目前在中国战场约有40个师，以及声称长江是向华中约100万军队供应物资的通道来看，可以判断出这一努力的规模。

因此，从最初被认为是一次相对局部的事件、仅需使用最小限度武力，日本已日益深陷其中，直至其使用的兵力表明她正参与一场大规模战争，而事实也确实如此。至于她已花费及正在花费的金额，以及这次冒险在其子民生命方面付出的代价，无法确定确切数字。伤亡报告被怀疑大幅缩水，但从日本领导人不时发表的各种声明中可以推断，金钱成本大约在150亿日元的实际支出左右，此外还有难以估算的贸易损失等。为了抵消这一点，有必要考虑她的收益。随着海岸线完全处于日本控制之下，中国贸易受到了扼制，国家的经济生活遭受了沉重打击。诚然，部分贸易可以通过缅甸路线和与苏联俄罗斯的陆路进行，军事补给也可以通过相同手段获得，但这两条渠道都有其劣势，特别是在需要考虑快速交付时尤为明显。但这也就是日本人所得到的全部。诚然，他们能够在长江上进行一定量的商业活动，

pages.en:
and are in fact doing so to the exclusion of
everyone else, but it is to be doubted whe-
ther, in view of the devastation which has
been wrought, and the consequent reduced
purchasing power of the Chinese, there is
very much profit in it in view of the huge
outlay to which Japan has been forced. For
the rest the military position appears to be
one of stalemate. The incursion into China
as far as the railways lines mentioned was
not, even making allowance for the resistance
of the Chinese really a particularly difficult
feat: it would have been much more difficult
had the Chinese possessed anything like the
equipment of the invaders. Chiang Kai-shek
and his government have withdrawn into
the western fastnesses, which he always con-
templated doing, and, though he and his
forces can be reached by means of aero-
planes, the sending in of adequate troops to
bring finality to the struggle is an entirely
different proposition.
The Japanese boast that there is not now
a spot in China which cannot be reached by
air is probably true, but experience of the
last few years has convincingly shown that
a country cannot be subjugated by such
means, and that ultimate victory depends
upon the bayonet, and armies of occupation.
It has been demonstrated that the areas
through which the Japanese have passed are
not in any real sense of the word occupied.
In the portion of China which is nominally
under Japanese control the greater portion
has not been really subdued, while the two
provisional governments set up in Nanking
and Peiping have no effective jurisdic-
tion beyond the range of a Japanese
rifle. Thus militarily a position of stalemate
has been reached, with, so far as it is
humanly possible to judge, very small pro-
spects of its being broken in the near future.
Indeed the only chance of this coming about
seems to lie in the possibility of there being
some disruption within the ranks of the
Chinese Government, of which there appears
to be no sign at present. The defection of
Wang Ching-wei has not proved to be the
severe blow to the Chiang Kai-shek régime
that some quarters appeared to believe, and
it is by no means improbable that the man-
ner in which that régime has withstood the
shock of it means that in effect it amounted
to accession of strength rather than of weak-
ness. That is apparently recognized in Japan
where the possibility of this struggle con-
tinuing another two years has now been
openly admitted in authoritative quarters.
If it is hoped by the Japanese, as appears
to be the case, that they will recoup much
of their expenditure by the exploitation of
the country there is the possibility that even
in this connection they are likely to be ser-
iously disappointed. Passive resistance on
the part of the Chinese, of which they are
past masters, must inevitably contribute to
that disappointment, and, if there are many
in Japan who are asking whether after all
the outlay in life, and treasure during
the last two years has been profitable, it is
not to be wondered at.

并且实际上正在这样做，排除了其他所有人；但鉴于所造成的破坏以及由此导致的中国人购买力下降，考虑到日本被迫承担的巨大开支，其中是否有太多利润值得怀疑。其余方面，军事局势似乎处于僵持状态。入侵中国直至上述铁路线，即使考虑到中国人的抵抗，也并非特别困难的壮举：如果中国人拥有类似入侵者的装备，那就会困难得多。蒋介石及其政府已撤退至西部险要地区，这是他一直预想会做的；虽然可以通过飞机联系到他和他的部队，但派遣足够的部队以给斗争带来最终结局则是完全不同的另一回事。
日本人吹嘘说，现在中国没有哪个地方是飞机无法到达的，这可能是真的；但过去几年的经验令人信服地表明，一个国家不能通过这种方式被征服，最终胜利取决于刺刀和占领军。事实证明，日军经过的地区在真正意义上并未被占领。在名义上受日本控制的中国部分地区中，大部分并未真正被征服，而在南京和北平设立的两个临时政府，其有效管辖权不出日本步枪射程之外。因此，军事上已达到僵持局面，就人力所能判断而言，近期打破这种局面的前景非常渺茫。事实上，实现这一点的唯一机会似乎在于中国政府内部可能出现某种分裂，而目前看来并无此迹象。汪精卫的叛变并未像某些方面所认为的那样，对蒋介石政权造成严重打击；毫不奇怪的是，该政权抵御这一冲击的方式意味着，实际上这反而增强了其力量而非削弱。这一点在日本似乎也得到承认，权威人士现已公开承认这场斗争可能再持续两年。如果日本人希望（情况似乎确实如此）通过剥削该国来收回其大部分支出，那么在这方面他们也很可能会严重失望。中国人擅长的消极抵抗必然会导致这种失望；如果有许多日本人询问，过去两年在生命和财富上的巨大投入究竟是否有利可图，这也不足为奇。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

JUL 7 1939

Police Arrest Over
500 Suspects

Large scale raids and search
parties carried out by members
of the Shanghai Municipal
Police last night as a precau-
tionary measure on the eve of
the second anniversary of the
beginning of the war netted
well over 500 arrests. Most of
these suspects were arrested
while loitering in streets and
alleyways, while raids on
hotels and tea houses accounted
for the rest. Police from
Central station seized 143 of
these suspects, while raiding
squads from Pootoo Road
station arrested a total of 90.
No arms were seized during
any of the raids, according to
police authorities.

《字林西报》。

1939年7月7日

警方逮捕逾
500名嫌疑人

昨晚，上海公共租界警务处成员作为战争爆发两周年纪念日前夕的预防措施，进行了大规模突袭和搜查行动，抓获了超过500名被捕者。大多数嫌疑人在街道和巷弄中闲逛时被捕，其余则是在对旅馆和茶楼的突袭中被捕。据警方当局称，中央巡捕房抓获了其中的143名嫌疑人，而普陀路巡捕房的突袭小队共逮捕了90人。在任何一次突袭中均未缴获武器。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
19 37
JUL 7 1939

War Anniversary
Passing Quietly
French Shut Doorways
On Avenue Edward
Concession Side

With troops and police
out in force, especially in
the French Concession,
Shanghai has had little to
complain about today, the
second anniversary of the
opening of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities, except incon-
venience to traffic. A small
number of propaganda pam-
phlets have been found.
Few changes have been
made in the barricade scheme
adopted on other recent mobi-
lizations, with one major ex-
ception. This is the closing
of all doorways on the French
side of Avenue Edward VII, which
has been in effect since 11 p.m.
yesterday. Even the Shanghai
Evening Post staff had to come to
work by a back entrance this
morning.

Shooting In West
Six shots fired on Keswick
Road around 10 o'clock last night
caused a bit of a flurry, until it
turned out that they had been
fired by Mr. H. Chatel, French
resident of a house near Rockhill
Avenue, because he was tired of
seeing loot gatherers come
through the perimeter wire close
to his house.
Hungjao residents were also a
little worried last night, when
they heard firing. Residents of
houses to the west of the Hung-
jao Golf Club reported fifteen
shots in rapid succession fired
just before 10 p.m., to the north
of their homes. There were a
few more for an hour or so later,
and again a few in the early
hours of today. Whether they
had been fired by Japanese
troops, or by bandits wishing to
intimidate the farmers, could not
be ascertained this morning.

Pamphlets
The French police this morning
seized a few copies of pamphlet
newspapers not registered in the
Concession, but only for the non-
registration reason, as there was
little to complain about in them
as regards the political angle.
Pamphlets were found in the
Bubbling Well district, but in
very small numbers. Some were
of an anti-Japanese nature, and
some were of the pro-Wang
Ching-wei plus New Order plus
Peace Movement type.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》。
19 37
1939年7月7日

战争周年纪念日
平静度过
法租界关闭
爱多亚路
法方一侧门户

由于军队和警察大量出动，特别是在法租界，上海在今天——中日敌对行动爆发两周年纪念日——几乎没有什么可抱怨的，除了交通不便外。发现了少量宣传小册子。除一个主要例外外，最近几次动员中采用的路障方案几乎没有变化。这个例外是关闭爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）法方一侧的所有门户，该措施自昨晚11点起生效。甚至《上海晚邮报》的员工今天早上也不得不从后门进入上班。

西区枪声

昨晚10点左右，克色维克路（Keswick Road）响起的六声枪声引起了一阵小骚动，直到后来 выяснилось，这些枪是由住在洛克希尔路（Rockhill Avenue）附近一所房子的法国居民H. Chatel先生发射的，因为他厌倦了看到拾荒者穿过靠近他家的周界铁丝网。
昨晚，虹桥居民听到枪声时也感到有些担忧。虹桥高尔夫俱乐部西侧房屋的居民报告称，晚上10点前不久，在他们家北面连续快速射出了十五发子弹。大约一小时后又响了几枪，今天凌晨又响了几枪。今早尚无法查明这些枪声是由日军还是由企图恐吓农民的匪徒所发射。

小册子

法警今早查获了几份未在租界注册的小册子报纸，但仅因未注册原因予以没收，因为从政治角度来看，这些小册子没什么可指责的。在静安寺地区发现了小册子，但数量极少。其中一些具有反日性质，另一些则属于亲汪精卫加“新秩序”加“和平运动”类型。

pages.en:
19□□

Bridges Guarded
British troops were on patrol
in certain parts of Central and
Louza districts, and for once
mounted guards on the Chapoo
and Szechuen Road bridges, in
addition to the usual Garden
Bridge post. They were also on
patrol in their western sector, as
were the Italian Marines in
theirs, and the US Marines in
"C" Sector.
North of the Soochow Creek,
conditions were just the same as
usual. The amount of searching
was even less than on normal
days. Last night, however, there
was a little minor excitement
caused by the Japanese closing
the Soochow Creek bridges from
9.30 to 10, and again for a short
period later on.
Volunteers Out
Members of the Shanghai
Volunteer Corps are patrolling as
required today. The Armored Car
Company went out on a Dawn
Patrol in "C" and "D" sectors,
and again patrolled during the
tiffin hour. Further patrols are
scheduled for this evening, but
no decision has been taken yet
on any early "stand down" order.
Police Specials were out last
night and on duty again today.
One or two trolleybus and bus
routes have been curtailed or
altered. In the Concession and
Settlement, owing to the bar-
ricade arrangements, but general-
ly speaking traffic has been able
to move satisfactorily throughout
the day. Stricter curfew control
was in effect last night, and
several hundred persons detain-
ed.
pages.zh:
19□□

守卫桥梁
英军在中区与卢家湾区的某些地段巡逻，并除通常的外白渡桥岗哨外，一度在乍浦路桥和四川路桥部署了骑马卫兵。他们在其西部防区也进行了巡逻，意大利海军陆战队在其防区、美国海军陆战队在“C”区 likewise 进行了巡逻。
苏州河以北的情况与往常完全相同。搜查力度甚至比平日还要少。然而，昨晚因日军在9:30至10:00期间关闭苏州河上的桥梁，随后又短暂关闭了一次，引起了一点小小的骚动。
义勇队出动
上海义勇队（Shanghai Volunteer Corps）队员今日按要求进行巡逻。装甲车公司在“C”区和“D”区进行了黎明巡逻，并在午餐时间再次巡逻。今晚计划进行进一步巡逻，但尚未就任何提前“撤岗”命令作出决定。
特别警察昨晚出动，今日再次执勤。一两条电车和公共汽车路线已缩短或更改。在法租界和公共租界，由于路障安排，但总体而言，全天交通尚能令人满意地通行。昨晚实施了更严格的宵禁管制，数百人被拘留。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JUL 7 1930

A Sad Anniversary
TWO YEARS AGO TODAY an incident in
North China occurred, later to prove a
Far East equivalent of Sarajevo. This is dis-
tinctly not one of the anniversaries that it
will profit anybody to observe. Most of
Shanghai—particularly the police of both
foreign areas—will take an attitude resembling
that of the Black Crow of vaudeville fame who
just didn't want to hear any more about it.
In the interest of all the various nationali-
ties jammed together in this city, we trust
that the day will prove one of peace and quiet.
Shanghai is not the place for patriotic activi-
ties at the moment. Such enterprises can
only jeopardize the welfare of all who look
upon the place as a shelter and who wish to
preserve its independent and neutral status.
It will be impossible, however, for any to
forget the sad connotations of this anniver-
sary. The amount of treasure wasted, the
number of lives lost or ruined, have now passed
all computation. And for what? Boil down
the mountains of verbiage surrounding this
"holy crusade", this "move for a New Order in
East Asia", and one finds nothing but
militaristic ambition running rampant to the
destruction of two great peoples and the harm
of every other nation with any Far East in-
terest. Civilization and culture have nothing
in common with the methods employed or the
ends sought.
"Dangerous thoughts" these are indeed.
But can any sane thinker think otherwise?
We fail to see how. No quantity of fine words
can excuse the ruthless employment of bomb
and bayonet in such fashion and for no
clearly-defined purpose save the forceful
domination of one nation by another. No
amount of explanation can make sense of it
all. Nor can any amount of blind optimism
bring success to such a cause. China is, has
been and will remain China—the property of
the Chinese.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》

1930年7月7日

一个悲伤的纪念日
两年前的今天，华北发生了一起事件，后来被证明是远东版的萨拉热窝事件。这绝不是一个值得任何人去纪念的日子。上海的大多数人——尤其是两个外国租界的警察——将采取一种类似于杂耍名角“黑乌鸦”的态度，即根本不想再听到任何相关的事情。
为了挤在这座城市里的各个国籍人士的利益，我们希望这一天将是和平与宁静的一天。目前上海不是进行爱国活动的地方。此类举动只会危及所有视此地为庇护所并希望保持其独立和中立地位的人的福祉。
然而，任何人都无法忘记这个纪念日所蕴含的悲伤意味。浪费的财富之多，丧生或被毁掉的生命之数，如今已无法计算。而这又是为了什么？剥去围绕这场“神圣十字军东征”、这场“东亚新秩序运动”的重重辞藻，人们发现的不过是肆意妄为的军国主义野心，它毁灭了两个伟大的民族，并损害了每一个在远东有利益关系的国家。文明和文化与所使用的手段或所追求的目标毫无共同之处。
这些确实是“危险的思想”。但是，任何理智的思想家还能有其他想法吗？我们看不出有何其他可能。再多的华丽辞藻也无法为以如此方式、除了强行让一个国家支配另一个国家之外没有明确目的而无情地使用炸弹和刺刀的行为开脱。再多的解释也无法使这一切变得合理。再多的盲目乐观也无法给这样的事业带来成功。中国是、一直是、并将永远是中国——中国人的财产。

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

JUL 5 1939

Police Stations
Closing Gates

Early Beginning Made
In Precautions
For July 7

Gates at the entrances to some
of the Settlement Police Stations
were closed last night from 6 p.m.
to 6 a.m. as part of the precau-
tions being taken for the second
anniversary of the outbreak of
the Sino-Japanese war.

General arrangements for July
7, follow the same lines as the
precautions taken on other days
in recent months on which dis-
turbances might have been ex-
pected. Certain streets will be
barricaded. Police search parties
will function at certain spots.

American Marines, British
Troops, the Russian Regiment
SVC and French Troops will
maintain street patrols. The
Armoured Car Company of the
SVC will patrol, but the rest of
the Corps, will be on precau-
tionary which means going to of-
fice in uniform, ready to mobilise
in a moment's notice. Special
police will reinforce the regulars
in the usual manner.

North of the Creek, precau-
tionary measures have already
been put into effect by the Japan-
ese Naval Landing Party, who are
carrying out intensive searching
of pedestrians.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》

1939年7月5日

警察局
关闭大门

为7月7日防范措施
提早开始行动

作为对中日战争爆发两周年采取的预防措施的一部分，昨晚6点至次日早上6点，公共租界部分警察局入口处的大门被关闭。

7月7日的总体安排遵循近几个月来在可能发生骚乱的其他日子所采取的预防措施的相同路线。某些街道将设置路障。警察搜查队将在某些地点执行任务。

美国海军陆战队、英军、俄国团义勇队以及法军将进行街道巡逻。义勇队装甲车公司将进行巡逻，但义勇队其余成员将处于戒备状态，这意味着身着制服前往办公室，随时准备在短时间内动员。特别警察将以通常方式增援正规警察。

在苏州河以北，日本海军陆战队已经实施了预防措施，他们正在对行人进行密集搜查。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY,
JUL 4 1939
Japanese Plan Quiet Solemnity
In Observing War Anniversary
Quiet solemnity, designed to "bring home" to Shanghai's Japanese population the gravity of the situation now confronting Japan, will mark the observance here of the second anniversary of the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities on Friday, the Shanghai Mainichi reports.
An Imperial rescript, granted a year ago, will be read at the meetings to be held by various Japanese organizations early on Friday morning, when the articles of the National Spiritualization campaign will be recited by those present.
One Course Meal:
One course meals will be offered at Japanese public eating places, while contributions to the National Defense Fund will be received at the Nippon Club and by members of the Japanese Women's Emergency Committee who will carry contribution boxes on the streets "Comfort bags," containing gifts to soldiers and sailors, for distribution at the front will also be accepted at the Club, and at the offices of Japanese textile and other firms as well as banks, the newspapers said.
Empty bottles, scrap iron, old blankets, newspapers, magazines, clothing and other discarded articles, suitable for remanufacture will be collected at the various Japanese primary schools on July 7 and 8, the paper added.

1939年7月4日
日本计划以肃穆安静的方式
纪念战争周年
据《上海每日新闻》报道，周五在此间纪念中日敌对行动爆发两周年时，将以安静的肃穆气氛为标志，旨在让上海的日本居民“深切体会”日本当前面临局势的严重性。
一年前颁布的一份帝国诏书，将在周五清晨由各个日本组织举行的会议上宣读，届时与会者将朗诵《国民精神总动员纲领》的条款。
单菜餐食：
日本的公共餐饮场所将提供单菜餐食，而在日本俱乐部以及日本妇女紧急委员会成员处将接收对国防基金的捐款，这些成员将在街头携带捐款箱。该报称，俱乐部以及日本纺织公司和其他公司及银行的办事处也将接受装有送给士兵和水手礼物的“慰问袋”，以便在前线分发。
该报补充说，7月7日和8日，将在各日本小学收集空瓶、废铁、旧毯子、报纸、杂志、衣物和其他适合再制造的废弃物品。

PEKING ECHO
JUL 7 1939

SECOND ANNIVERSARY

TODAY marks the second anniversary of the Sino-Japanese hostilities. In the annals of China and Japan, it will go down as the most memorable day. To the world generally, it will long be remembered as the day which may mark a turning point in Far Eastern history. The significance of the day in world's history, perhaps, will be better appreciated in the light of future events than what has already happened, for the hostilities in China, if unduly prolonged, are bound to have international repercussions. Whether the spark at Lukouchiao, two years ago today, that started the conflagration on the Far Eastern front will eventually lead to another world catastrophe, it is impossible to say. But the dangers of such an eventuality are lurking everywhere, especially in view of the fact that the various Powers are piling up armaments to get prepared for another carnage.

Those of us who have been eyewitnesses of the Sino-Japanese tragedy cannot but be pained at the events that had transpired during the past two years. If it were possible to summarize in one sentence what has happened, it can only be described as a period of bloodshed and destruction. The years of hostilities have not settled anything in Sino-Japanese relations. It is indeed heart-rending to witness that the tragedy is still being enacted before our eyes and that no end of it is in sight.

In this tragedy, both China and Japan have been sufferers. The only difference between them is the extent of suffering endured by each. Since the war has been fought on Chinese soil, naturally China has been the greater victim, but Japan has also undergone heavy sacrifices in men and resources, which must have a deleterious effect on the Japanese nation. As a neutral observer, we are at a complete loss to understand why the two Oriental countries, which are in many ways congruous and should have been harmonious, cannot settle their differences by pacific means instead of choosing to stake everything in a war of mutual attrition. Perhaps, many will agree with us in the view that unless the leaders of both countries responsible for the prolongation of the hostilities realize the consequences of their actions and mend their ways, posterities of both nations will not pardon them for the calamities they will have brought about.

In reviewing the events of the past two years, one is struck by horror and dismay at the extent of bloodshed and destruction. The casualties, military and civilian, caused by the hostilities, have been appalling. They are believed to run into a colossal figure. Millions of war refugees have been deprived of homes and whatever they had and are now reduced to beggary. Material destruction has been so immense that it defies calculation. Hundreds of once prosperous cities have been levelled to the ground, wide-spread areas in China's vast hinterland converted into an expanse of wreckage, with nothing left but debris, death and disease. Such is the grim picture of China one sees at the end of these two years of hostilities. It is a picture too grim to be believable.
pages.zh:
《北平回声报》
1939年7月7日

两周年

今天标志着中日敌对行动的两周年。在中日两国的史册中，这将成为最难忘的一天。对整个世界而言，它将长期被人们铭记为可能标志着远东历史转折点的一天。也许，结合未来的事件，而非仅凭已发生的事情，人们能更好地领会这一天在世界历史上的意义，因为如果中国的敌对行动过度延长，必然会产生国际反响。两年前今天在卢沟桥点燃远东战线大火的火花最终是否会导致另一场世界性灾难，目前尚不可知。但这种可能性的危险潜伏在各处，特别是鉴于各国正在堆积军备，为另一场屠杀做准备。

我们这些中日悲剧的目击者，不能不对过去两年发生的事件感到痛心。如果可以用一句话来概括所发生的一切，那只能描述为一段流血和破坏的时期。多年的敌对行动并未解决中日关系中的任何问题。目睹悲剧仍在我们要眼前上演且看不到尽头，确实令人心碎。

在这场悲剧中，中国和日本都是受害者。两者之间的唯一区别是各自承受苦难的程度。由于战争是在中国领土上进行的，中国自然成为了更大的受害者，但日本也在人力和资源方面遭受了重大牺牲，这必然对日本民族产生有害影响。作为中立的观察者，我们完全无法理解，为什么这两个在许多方面相契合、本应和谐相处的东方国家，不能通过和平手段解决分歧，而是选择在一场相互消耗的战争中孤注一掷。也许，许多人会同意我们的观点，除非两国对延长敌对行动负责的领导人认识到其行为的后果并改正做法，否则后代不会原谅他们带来的灾难。

回顾过去两年的事件，人们会对流血和破坏的程度感到震惊和惊恐。敌对行动造成的军民伤亡令人震惊。据信数字巨大。数百万战争难民失去了家园和所有财产，如今沦为乞丐。物质破坏如此巨大，以至于无法计算。数百座曾经繁荣的城市被夷为平地，中国广阔内地的广大地区变成了一片废墟，只剩下残骸、死亡和疾病。这就是在中日敌对行动两年结束时人们看到的中国的严峻景象。这是一幅严峻得令人难以置信的画面。

pages.en:
The hostilities started this day two years ago due to
what was really a misunderstanding. But the misunder-
standing arose mainly out of the presence of Japanese troops
at Lukouchiao. The circumstances of the so-called Lukou-
chiao Incident into which we will not enter are rather com-
plicated and controversial, but according to the Japanese a
mysterious shot was fired by some unknown person in the
dead of night when Japanese troops were conducting
manoeuvres and a Japanese soldier was missing. The
Japanese immediately demanded entrance to the nearby
town of Wanping to search for the mysterious sharpshooter
and rejection of their demand by the Chinese garrison of
the city precipitated the first clash.
Immediately following the occurrence of the incident,
efforts were made by both Chinese and Japanese representa-
tives at Peiping to reach a peaceful settlement, but such
efforts failed and the incident became daily aggravated. The
situation took a serious turn on July 25, when Lt.-Gen. K.
Katsuki delivered an ultimatum to Gen. Sung Cheh-yuan,
Commander of the 29th Route Army at Peiping, demanding
the withdrawal of all Chinese troops from the ancient
capital within 48 hours. Following rejection of the ulti-
matum by Gen. Sung, the Japanese Army immediately
commenced operations. The fall of Peiping and Tientsin
by the end of July and the consequent extension of hostili-
ties into other parts of North China dashed to pieces all
hopes of localising the conflict and made large-scale hostili-
ties inevitable. On August 13, the war spread to Shanghai
and by the beginning of September, practically all the coastal
provinces were involved.
Wars are futile and never settle things permanently.
The last World War, as events during the past decade have
proved, did not solve the European muddle, but only sowed
seeds of future conflicts. We hope that our apprehension
that the Far Eastern blaze might light up another general
conflagration is ill-founded; otherwise, the consequence to
the world's civilization will be too terrible to imagine.
pages.zh:
两年前的今天，敌对行动始于实际上是一场误会。但这场误会主要源于日军在卢沟桥的存在。所谓“卢沟桥事变”的情况相当复杂且充满争议，我们在此不深入探讨，但据日方称，在深夜日军进行演习时，一名不明身份的人发射了一发神秘的子弹，且一名日本士兵失踪。日军立即要求进入附近的宛平城搜寻那名神秘的神枪手，中国守军拒绝了这一要求，从而引发了第一次冲突。
事件发生后，中日双方代表在北平立即努力寻求和平解决，但这些努力失败了，事态日益恶化。7月25日，局势发生了严重转折，香月清司中将向北平第29军军长宋哲元将军发出最后通牒，要求在48小时内将所有中国军队撤出古都。宋将军拒绝最后通牒后，日军立即开始行动。7月底北平和天津的陷落，以及随之而来的敌对行动向中国华北其他地区的扩展，粉碎了将冲突局部化的所有希望，并使大规模敌对行动成为不可避免。8月13日，战争蔓延至上海，到9月初，几乎所有沿海省份都被卷入其中。
战争是徒劳的，永远不能永久解决问题。正如过去十年的事件所证明的那样，上一次世界大战并没有解决欧洲的混乱局面，只是播下了未来冲突的种子。我们希望我们对远东大火可能引发另一场全面战争的担忧是没有根据的；否则，对世界文明的后果将可怕得难以想象。

CHINA PRESS.
JUL 8 1939
19560
Japan Seeks End Of
Foreign Rights In
China, Chiang Warns

Leader Says China Will
Fight On Until Japan
Abandons Invasion

MADAME CHIANG
BROADCASTS TALK

Nippon Said Exhausted;
Threats Merely
Empty Boasts

(United Press)
CHUNGKING, July 7.—
Warning that Japan's inten-
tion of creating a "new order
in East Asia" was an open
challenge to the Powers
friendly to China and aimed
at driving their rights and
interests from China, Gen-
eralissimo Chiang Kai-shek
tonight in a radio broadcast
to the world called on the
Powers to apply economic
sanctions against Japan.
The Generalissimo's address to
the world on second anniversary of
the outbreak of hostilities was broad-
cast tonight by Madame Chiang
Kai-shek.
China will not conclude her
resistance against Japanese ag-
gression until Japan thoroughly
abandons its policy of aggres-
sion, the Generalissimo said.
He pointed out that Japan, by ob-
taining materials from abroad, was
aided in employing brute force
against China's innocent population
and thus also endangered foreign
property rights in China.
The combined pressure of
sanctions against Japan by the
Powers and China's own
strength and resistance would
bring about the downfall of
Japan and thus protect the
rights and interests in China of
the Third Party nations, he said.
Japan Exhausted
The Generalissimo claimed Japan
has reached a point of exhaustion
and that the threats of Japanese
militarists "are merely empty
boasts."
He traced the present anarchy
and international disorder to
Japan's forcible seizure of Man-
churia in 1931, and asserted that
there was still a path open to halt-
ing Japan's ambitions.
Gen. Chiang's broadcast follows:
"On the eve of the Lukouchiao
incident the world still half doubt-
ed whether the Japanese militar-
ists were really bent on conquering
China and the world.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。
1939年7月8日
19560
蒋介石警告：日本寻求终结
在华外国权益

领袖称中国将抗战到底，
直至日本放弃侵略

宋美龄发表广播讲话

据称日本已筋疲力尽；
威胁仅是空洞吹嘘

（合众社）
重庆，7月7日电——蒋介石委员长今晚在向全世界发表的广播讲话中警告说，日本意图建立“东亚新秩序”是对与中国友好的列强的公开挑战，旨在将其权利和利益驱逐出中国，并呼吁列强对日本实施经济制裁。
适逢战事爆发两周年之际，蒋委员长向全世界发表的演说今晚由宋美龄女士广播。
蒋委员长表示，在日本彻底放弃其侵略政策之前，中国不会停止对日本侵略的抵抗。
他指出，日本通过从国外获取物资，得以对中国无辜民众使用暴力，从而也危及了外国在华财产权益。
他说，列强对日本施加的制裁压力与中国自身的力量和抵抗相结合，将导致日本的垮台，从而保护第三国在华的权利和利益。
日本已筋疲力尽
蒋委员长声称，日本已达到筋疲力尽的地步，日本军国主义者的威胁“仅是空洞的吹嘘”。
他将目前的无政府状态和国际混乱归咎于日本在1931年强行夺取满洲，并断言仍有途径可以遏制日本的野心。
蒋将军的广播讲话如下：
“在卢沟桥事变前夕，世界仍半信半疑，不确定日本军国主义者是否真的决心征服中国和世界。

pages.en:
Japan's Intentions
"Now such Japanese national policy has turned out to be an irrefutable fact. Moreover, the world also has come to realize that the state of international lawlessness, disorder and anarchy are the consequences of Japan's forcible seizure of China's four Northeastern Provinces.
"Since the issuance of the statement on the new order in East Asia by the Prince Konoye cabinet last December, it has been further proved that the Japanese invasion of China, no matter under what pretenses, has as its real object the expulsion of European and American rights and interests from Asia so as to pave the way for the consummation of Japan's ambition of proclaiming a hegemony over the Pacific.
"Determined to continue to employ force to defeat Japanese aggression, China will neither turn back nor call off her resistance before the enemy has thoroughly abandoned its policy of aggression despite greater sacrifices and privations.
"Her stand is bound to have a tremendous effect on the future of world order and welfare of mankind."
"Since the armistice following the European War, friendly nations contributed their utmost to the cause of peace. As embodied in the League of Nations covenant, the Kellogg-Briand Pact and the Nine Power treaty. However, Japan's military action against China constitutes outright contravention of these treaties.
"The Chinese people, however, are gratified by the fact that the proponents of these pacts have not wavered from support of the sanctity of treaties in spite of repeated intimidations by Japanese militarists, to the Western countries in the hope of driving out the latter's rights and interests from East Asia and prior to setting up their so-called 'New Order.'"
Cunning Trick
"This clearly shows that Japan openly challenges China's friendly powers and does not hesitate to assume the role of ringleader.
"In this concerted onslaught on nations friendly to China, the Japanese militarists are resorting to the cunning trick of breaking up each power separately. They have not only insulted Third Party nationals and seized Third Party property in China but have also wantonly destroyed Third Party missionary, cultural and economic institutions and needlessly killed those serving these institutions.
"The fact remains that after two years of resistance put up by China, the enemy has gradually reached a point of exhaustion and is no longer able to exert pressure on any other country.
"Threats of the Japanese militarists are merely empty boasts. I deeply believe the friendly powers who love peace and uphold justice will not be deceived by these empty boasts of the Japanese militarists or frightened by their militant measures.
"Inasmuch as China is not fighting for her national independence alone, the peoples and the governments of friendly powers should no longer defer taking action on the unanimous demand of the Chinese nation by utilizing the authority contained in international treaties and enforcing effective economic measures against Japan."
pages.zh:
日本的意图
“如今，这种日本国策已被证实为无可辩驳的事实。此外，世界也已认识到，国际无法无天、混乱和无政府的状态是日本强行夺取中国东北四省的后果。
“自去年12月近卫文麿内阁发表关于东亚新秩序的声明以来，进一步证明日本侵华无论以何种借口为掩饰，其真实目的都是将欧美在华权益驱逐出亚洲，以便为日本实现宣称太平洋霸权的野心铺平道路。
“中国决心继续运用武力击败日本侵略，在敌人彻底放弃其侵略政策之前，尽管牺牲和困苦更大，中国既不会后退，也不会停止抵抗。
“中国的立场必将对世界秩序的未来和人类福祉产生巨大影响。”
“自欧洲大战停战以来，友好国家为和平事业尽了最大努力。这体现在《国际联盟盟约》、《凯洛格-白里安公约》和《九国公约》中。然而，日本对华军事行动构成了对这些条约的公然违反。
“然而，令中国人民感到欣慰的是，尽管日本军国主义者反复恐吓西方国家，希望将后者的权益驱逐出东亚并在建立其所谓‘新秩序’之前，这些公约的倡导者并未动摇对条约神圣性的支持。”
狡猾伎俩
“这清楚地表明，日本公开挑战中国的友好强国，并毫不犹豫地充当头目角色。
“在对华友好国家的协同攻击中，日本军国主义者正采取各个击破的狡猾伎俩。他们不仅侮辱在华第三国国民并没收第三国财产，还肆意破坏第三国的传教、文化和经济机构，并无端杀害在这些机构服务的人员。
“事实是，经过中国两年的抵抗，敌人已逐渐达到筋疲力尽的地步，不再能够对任何其他国家施加压力。
“日本军国主义者的威胁仅是空洞的吹嘘。我深信，热爱和平、主持正义的友好强国不会被日本军国主义者的这些空洞吹嘘所欺骗，也不会被其好战措施所吓倒。
“既然中国不仅仅是为民族独立而战，友好强国的人民和政府就不应再推迟行动，而应利用国际条约中所载的权力，对日本采取有效的经济措施，以响应中国国民的一致要求。”

pages.en:
Economic Sanctions Urged
"It is common knowledge abroad
that money obtained by Japan's
purchase of petrol, iron, steel and
other war materials helps to aug-
ment the brute force which will not
only aid Japan's onslaught on the
innocent Chinese but further en-
danger foreign property rights in
China.
"If friendly nations imme-
diately adopt effective economic
sanctions against Japan and at
the same time increase their
material assistance to China,
there is every assurance that
China's own strength plus this
international pressure will bring
the downfall of Japan's mili-
tarists within a short period and
help to restore the efficacy of
various international conven-
tions as well as promote ever-
lasting world peace and human
welfare.
"Should the powers hesitate or
compromise in the hope of saving
themselves it is tantamount to en-
couraging aggression...
"If at the outbreak of the
Mukden Incident the signatories of
the League of Nations covenant and
the Nine Power Pact had taken re-
solute action against Japan, the
world would not have been threaten-
ed by an imminent outbreak of an-
other conflagration.
Still Not Too Late
"Nevertheless, it is still not too
late if friendly powers can apply
joint action against Japan im-
mediately. Otherwise, the im-
pending international catas-
trophe will be unavoidable.
"China has been a peace-living
nation for 5,000 years and will
exert still greater efforts to con-
tribute to world peace and justice.
"We believe China with a
population of 450,000,000 people will
make a substantial contribution to
international order and prosperity
and will not disappoint those lend-
ing us a helping hand.
"No matter whether now or in
the future, China will need the
help of her friends and likewise they
will need the help of China."
pages.zh:
呼吁经济制裁
“海外众所周知，日本购买汽油、铁、钢和其他战争物资所得的资金，有助于增强其暴力力量，这不仅助长日本对无辜中国人的攻击，还进一步危及外国在华财产权益。
“如果友好国家立即对日本采取有效的经济制裁，同时增加对中国的物质援助，那么完全可以保证，中国自身的力量加上这种国际压力，将在短期内导致日本军国主义的垮台，并有助于恢复各种国际公约的效力，促进永恒的世界和平与人类福祉。
“如果列强犹豫不决或妥协，希望能保全自己，这无异于鼓励侵略……
“如果在‘九一八’事变爆发时，《国际联盟盟约》和《九国公约》的签署国对日本采取坚决行动，世界就不会受到另一场战火即将爆发的威胁。
为时未晚
“尽管如此，如果友好强国能立即对日本采取联合行动，现在为时未晚。否则，迫在眉睫的国际灾难将不可避免。
“中国是一个爱好和平的国家已有5000年历史，并将付出更大努力为世界和平与正义作出贡献。
“我们相信，拥有4.5亿人口的中国将为国际秩序与繁荣作出实质性贡献，绝不会让那些向我们伸出援手的人失望。
“无论现在还是将来，中国都需要朋友的帮助，同样，他们也需要中国的帮助。”

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS.
JUL 3 1939
No Terrorism
Develops Here
On Anniversary
Day Passes Without
Incident; Forces
Demobilized
July 7, the second anniversary of
the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hos-
tilities, passed in Shanghai without
serious incident, local Settlement
and French Concession police quar-
ters revealed last night.
Not a single case of terrorism was
reported during the day. Nothing
of this sort was expected, of course,
but considering the fact that July
7, 1938, was featured by almost a
dozen bombings and shootings, the
authorities reasoned that anything
might happen and general mobili-
zation of police and military forces
in both foreign administered areas
of the city was ordered.
Troops Out In Force
British troops, American marines
and Italian bluejackets as well as
police reserves and specials were out
in force in the International Settle-
ment, while the Shanghai Volunteer
Corps was mobilized at 5.30 p.m. and
kept on duty until after 9 o'clock.
General demobilization of all police
and military forces in the Settle-
ment was ordered at 10 p.m. and
the barbed wire barricades along
Avenue Edward VII and Avenue
Foch street intersections commenced
to make their disappearance. The
majority of the barriers are ex-
pected to be down by dawn.
Precautionary measures taken in
the French Concession were still in
force early this morning but it is
understood that the French police
specials and volunteers will be
demobilized early today. Barricades
on the French Concession side of
Avenue Edward VII were still in
place at 1 a.m. today. The French
police also rigidly enforced curfew
regulations last night as did the
Settlement authorities.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。
1939年7月3日
此地周年纪念
未发生恐怖活动
当日平安无事；
部队复员
7月7日是中日敌对行动爆发两周年纪念日，上海当日未发生严重事件，本地公共租界和法租界警察分局昨晚透露。
全天未报告一起恐怖案件。当然，人们并未预料到此类事件，但鉴于1938年7月7日发生了近十起爆炸和枪击事件，当局认为任何事情都可能发生，因此下令在全市两个外籍管理区域全面动员警察和军事力量。
部队大规模出动
英国军队、美国海军陆战队和意大利水兵以及警察后备队和特务人员在公共租界大规模出动，而上海万国商团于下午5点30分动员，并执勤至晚上9点以后。
晚上10点，下令对租界内所有警察和军事力量进行总复员，沿爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）和霞飞路（Avenue Foch）交叉口的铁丝网路障开始拆除。预计大多数路障将在黎明前撤除。
法租界采取的预防措施今天清晨仍然有效，但据悉法国警察特务人员和志愿者将于今天早些时候复员。今天凌晨1点，爱多亚路法租界一侧的路障仍在原位。法国警察昨晚也像租界当局一样严格执行宵禁规定。

pages.en:
1958

One Shooting Case
One incident involving the firing
of about six shots occurred on Kes-
wick Road late Thursday evening.
Investigation revealed that Mr. H.
Chatei, French tenant of a house
near Rockhill Avenue, fired the
shots into the air because he was
tired of watching looters come
through the perimeter wire close
to his home.
Some guerilla activity was report-
ed in the Hungjao area late Thurs-
day night and early yesterday
morning. Foreign residents of this
district stated that they heard heavy
shooting about 10 a.m. Thursday
and again early Friday morning.
French police reported a few cases
in which pro-Chinese leaflets had
been distributed but no incidents of
this sort occurred in the Settlement.

Shops Closed
One of the interesting develop-
ments of the day was the fact that
all Chinese shops along Avenue
Edward VII on the French Conces-
sion side of the street were literally
closed from early morning until late
last night. They were not closed
because the merchants wanted them
closed but rather because the
French police authorities barricaded
the front entrances. If business
was to be done during the day, said
the French police, it would have to
be done through the back door. The
idea, according to French police offi-
cials, was to prevent terrorists from
making their escape from the street
through shop entrances.
Three wounded Chinese were
brought into the Settlement yester-
day from Japanese occupied terri-
tory. Two came in through the
Western District barriers while one
was transported across the Whang-
poo River from Pootung. The latter
is said to have been wounded by
armed robbers two days ago. Just
who is responsible for the wounding
of the two men who came through
the western barriers is unknown.
pages.zh:
1958

一起枪击案
周四深夜，在祁齐路（Keswick Road）发生一起涉及约六声枪响的事件。调查显示，罗高路（Rockhill Avenue）附近一所房屋的法国租户H. Chatei先生（音译）向空中开枪，因为他厌倦了看着劫掠者穿过靠近他家的周边铁丝网。
据报道，周四深夜和昨天清晨，虹桥地区发生了一些游击队活动。该地区的外国居民表示，他们在周四上午10点左右和周五清晨听到了激烈的枪声。
法国警察报告了几起分发亲华传单的案件，但公共租界内未发生此类事件。

商店关闭
当天一个有趣的发展是，法租界一侧爱多亚路沿线的所有中国商店实际上从清晨到昨晚深夜一直关闭。它们关闭并非因为商人想关门，而是因为法国警察当局封锁了前门入口。法国警察称，如果白天要做生意，就必须走后门。据法国警察官员称，此举旨在防止恐怖分子通过商店入口从街道逃脱。
昨天有三名受伤的中国人从日军占领区被带入公共租界。其中两人通过西区路障进入，另一人从浦东经黄浦江运送过来。据说后者是两天前被武装抢劫者打伤的。至于通过西部路障进入的两名男子受伤的责任人是谁，目前尚不清楚。

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS.
JUL 7 1939
Optimism Prevails In China, But Pessimism
Grips Japan On An niversary, Writer Sta

Stern Preparations For
Long Conflict Said
Pushed In Tokyo

By ALFRED LUSK
(Special To THE CHINA PRESS)
As two years of bitter Sino-
Japanese hostilities came to a close
on July 7, the War Office in Tokyo
issued half a million copies of a
bellicose pamphlet declaring that
“In order to achieve the great task
of constructing a new order in East
Asia, we must be prepared to take
50 or even 100 years.”
Almost simultaneously, from
Chungking, depopulated and badly
torn by Japanese bombs, came a
statement predicting that the war
would end in a victory for China
“within three or five years.”
The two declarations were a
significant reflection of the senti-
ment prevailing in the two capitals
after two years of fighting. Having
reached the geographical limits of
conquest without breaking China’s
will to resist, Japan is beginning to
realize that the seizure of a large
section of Chinese territory had not
given her victory.
Tokyo no longer speaks of the
imminent collapse of what it des-
cribes as “the Chiang Kai-shek
regime.” There is a stern-faced
preparation for hostilities of indefi-
nite duration, a mobilization of
labor and capital, reduced con-
sumption and wages and intensified
production of munitions. There are
also efforts to stimulate the waning
public morale by such means as the
landing in Swatow and exacerba-
tion of relations with Britain.
Chinese Optimistic
Paradoxically, it is in ravaged
China where hope and optimism
rule supreme. The Chinese believe
that the Japanese war machine has
become mired in the vast spaces of
the occupied territory, and that the
lean Tokyo coffers cannot afford
the tremendous cost of keeping this
machine in action.
The Japanese, Chungking holds,
have reached the outer rim of the
territory in which they can use
with advantage their heavy artillery
and mechanized units. They have
now reached the tall and rugged
mountainous belt extending from
Inner Mongolia to Indo-China,
where tanks and heavy guns can
no longer be employed. Japan has
thus lost the only factor which had
assured her military superiority
over China.
The Japanese armed forces—and
this is one of the most important
features of the situation today—
have lost the initiative they had
enjoyed up to the capture of Han-
kow, late in October, 1938. They
have now been thrown on the de-
fensive, with their rear and dan-
gerously extended supply routes ex-
posed to guerilla attack.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》。
1939年7月7日
作家斯塔恩称：中国乐观情绪占上风，但日本在周年纪念日陷入悲观

东京据称正加紧为长期冲突做严峻准备

阿尔弗雷德·拉斯克 撰
（《字林西报》特约稿）
随着两年惨烈的中日敌对行动于7月7日告一段落，东京陆军省发布了五十万份好战小册子，宣称“为了完成构建东亚新秩序的伟大任务，我们必须做好五十年甚至一百年的准备。”
几乎与此同时，从被日军炸弹炸得人口锐减、满目疮痍的重庆传来一份声明，预测战争将在“三至五年内”以中国的胜利告终。
这两项宣言显著反映了经过两年战斗后两国首都 prevailing 的情绪。日本在达到征服的地理极限却未能摧毁中国的抵抗意志后，开始意识到占领大片中国领土并未给它带来胜利。
东京不再提及它所描述的“蒋介石政权”即将崩溃。取而代之的是为无限期的敌对行动进行严阵以待的准备，动员劳动力和资本，削减消费和工资，并加强军火生产。此外，还试图通过登陆汕头以及加剧与英国的关系等手段，来提振日益低落的公众士气。
中国人保持乐观
具有讽刺意味的是，在饱受蹂躏的中国，希望和乐观情绪占据主导地位。中国人认为，日本的战争机器已陷入占领区广阔空间的泥潭，而东京空虚的国库无法承担维持这台机器运转的巨大成本。
重庆方面认为，日本人已经到达了能够有效使用其重炮和机械化部队的领土外缘。他们现在到达了从内蒙古延伸至印度支那的高大崎岖的山脉地带，在那里坦克和重炮已无法使用。因此，日本失去了确保其对中国军事优势的唯一因素。
日本武装部队——这是当今局势最重要的特征之一——已经失去了直到1938年10月下旬攻占汉口之前所享有的主动权。他们现在被迫转入防御，其后部和危险地延长的补给线暴露在游击队的攻击之下。

pages.en:
The war, the Chinese hold, has
now degenerated into a contest of
endurance, in which agricultural
China has an edge over industrial-
ized Nippon. There are dangerous
stresses in Japanese economy,
which to Chungking appear to be
signs of a major economic, and
consequently political, crisis within
the next few years. In this, the
Chinese, despite their own difficul-
ties, see hope of eventual victory.
Military Situation Outlined
The military situation on July 7
was as follows:—
Japanese troops were thickly
massed along a 1,000-mile straight
line linking destroyed Canton, the
capital of South China, with Pei-
ping. The Japanese Navy was
stretched along an arch embracing
the entire sea-coast, from Korea to
French Indo-China.
Within this gigantic segment,
there was a political vacuum, rela-
tively free of the Japanese and
governed either by the administra-
tive machinery which had survived
the shock of war or by new ma-
chinery set up by guerillas.
All the major cities—Peiping,
Tientsin, Tsinan, Tsingtao, Taiyuan,
Hsuchow, Hankow, Shanghai, Nan-
king, Amoy, and Canton—were
under Japanese military rule and
gave refuge to various puppet re-
gimes established by the invading
army.
The authority of these adminis-
trative organs, despite the support
afforded by the Japanese Fighting
Services and banks, did not extend
beyond the cities and towns garri-
soned by the Japanese. And even
in these cities, the lives of the pro-
Japanese officials were in constant
danger, as was demonstrated by the
attempted poisoning of the leaders
of the Nanking regime early in
June at a banquet in the Japanese
consulate-general.
Japan's task now was not to
extend the limits of the area under
her flag, but to bring the segment
under complete control, permitting
the commencement of economic ex-
ploitation of the occupied territory.
At the same time, however, Japan
had to maintain a constant vigil
along the rims of the seized area,
to prevent the infiltration of Chin-
ese troops from their bases in the
rich and inaccessible westernmost
provinces.

Number Grows

To carry these plans into
life, Japan is now keeping roughly
1,200,000 men under arms through-
out China proper. Tokyo claimed
in April that it had 1,000,000 men
in Central China alone, but this
was apparently an attempt to
frighten Chungking into a with-
drawal of its forces from the
Shansi and other fronts. It could
be assumed with fair accuracy that
Japan today maintains armies of
half-a-million men in Central and
North China each, in addition to
a force scattered throughout South
China.
This number has thus far proved
sufficient to prevent Chinese recap-
ture of the occupied territory, but
totally inadequate for the Hercu-
lean task of destroying the new
Chinese bases beyond the moun-
tains of Shansi, Szechwan, Kwei-
chow and Kwangsi or for estab-
lishing peace in the invaded areas.
The Chinese, on the other hand,
had under arms on July 7 an
undetermined number of men,
ranging between 2,000,000 and
3,000,000, of whom 1,000,000 were
fresh troops operating from bases
in "Free China" and the rest were
regulars and guerillas fighting
within the occupied provinces.
pages.zh:
中国人认为，战争现已退化为一场耐力竞赛，在这场竞赛中，农业中国比工业化的日本占有优势。日本经济存在危险的紧张局势，在重庆看来，这是未来几年内发生重大经济危机乃至政治危机的迹象。在这方面，尽管中国人自身面临困难，但他们看到了最终胜利的希望。
军事形势概述
7月7日的军事形势如下：
日军密集部署在一条长达1000英里的直线上，连接着被毁的华南首府广州与北平。日本海军沿着一道弧线展开，涵盖了从朝鲜到法属印度支那的整个海岸线。
在这个巨大的扇形区域内，存在一个政治真空地带，相对没有日本人，由经受住战争冲击而幸存下来的行政机构，或由游击队建立的新机构进行管理。
所有主要城市——北平、天津、济南、青岛、太原、徐州、汉口、上海、南京、厦门和广州——均处于日本军事统治之下，并为入侵军队建立的各种傀儡政权提供庇护。
尽管有日本陆海军和银行的支持，这些行政机构的权力并未扩展到日军驻防的城镇之外。即使在这些城市里，亲日官员的生命也处于持续的危险之中，6月初在南京 regime 领导人在日本总领事馆举行的宴会上遭遇投毒未遂事件，便证明了这一点。
日本现在的任务不是扩大其旗帜下的区域范围，而是对该扇形区域实施完全控制，以便开始对占领区进行经济剥削。然而，与此同时，日本必须在占领区的边缘保持持续警戒，以防止中国军队从其位于富庶且难以进入的最西部省份的基地渗透进来。

人数增加

为了将这些计划付诸实施，日本目前在中国本土维持着约120万人的武装力量。东京在4月份声称仅在华中华地区就有100万军队，但这显然是一种试图恐吓重庆，使其从山西和其他战线撤军的企图。可以相当准确地假设，日本今天在华中和华北各维持着50万人的军队，此外还有一支部队分散在华南各地。
迄今为止，这一数量足以防止中国收复被占领土，但对于摧毁山西、四川、贵州和广西山脉以外的新中国基地或在 invaded 地区建立和平这项艰巨任务来说，则完全不足。
另一方面，中国在7月7日拥有的武装人员数量不定，介于200万至300万之间，其中100万是从“自由中国”基地作战的新兵，其余则是 within 被占领省份作战的正规军和游击队。

pages.en:
Cost Is Tremendous

The costs of Japan's armed venture in China cannot be estimated in terms of money alone, although these have been staggering. The war has retarded for a decade or two the incredible progress that was being witnessed in China between 1931 and 1937. It has compelled the migration of 50,000,000 Chinese from their homes to provinces often a thousand miles away. The war has destroyed in China cultural and social values defying monetary estimation. Possibly 1,500,000 Chinese had perished as the result of war. About a third of these were innocent civilians.

The nation's financial losses are also beyond evaluation at this time. Their extent, however, can be surmised by the fact that in Chapei alone the value of damaged or seized property was believed to exceed $1,000,000,000 in pre-war currency. Only two of China's major cities had escaped damage—Peiping and Tientsin (although there was some fierce fighting in the latter). Some of the others, such as Canton, Nanchang, Changsha, Hankow, Soochow and Hsuchow, were devastated by Japanese bombardment and by fires often started by the withdrawing Chinese. There can scarcely be a town in this vast land which had been spared by Japanese aerial raiders, who scattered their bombs with fine disregard for the objectives.

Losses Smaller

Japan's losses were incomparably smaller, because the war was fought on Chinese soil. Yet, even they were the largest in Japan's history. A very conservative estimate would put the number of Japanese uniformed men killed in China at 250,000, with three times that number wounded. Shipload after shipload of little ash-laden wooden boxes wrapped with white cloth is leaving China ports for Japan, there to be met by crying mothers, wives and children.

In terms of money, the "China Incident", has already cost the Japanese government nearly Y.12,000,000,000, or about seven times as much as the whole Russo-Japanese war. In addition, there have been enormous losses in the form of lost export markets, abandoned peace industries, unemployment, diversion of capital into non-productive industries, reduced agricultural and marine output, deterioration in the quality of produced goods, severely curtailed consumption and exhaustion of Japan's stock of specie.

There have also been such intangible losses, for instance, as the drop in the birth rate by 40 per cent during 1938, as the result of the mobilization of able-bodied males.

But most significant of all has been the drastic change in Japan's political and economic structure from relative liberalism and laissez faire to military regimentation not less rigid than that in Germany or Italy. Conscription of manpower and capital, already approved by the Cabinet, is the latest in the long series of army-backed moves in the direction of military fascism.

Chinese Determined

When the war started two years ago, Japan expected a quick victory over the ill-organized northern troops and a consequent tightening of her grip on North China's economic and political structure. China was desperately anxious to avert a war, but determined to check the disastrous "gobbling up" process, through which the Japanese Army was rapidly gnawing its way into the heart of this country.
pages.zh:
代价巨大

日本在华武装冒险的成本不能仅用金钱来估算，尽管这些数字令人震惊。这场战争使中国在1931年至1937年间见证的惊人进步推迟了一二十年。它迫使5000万中国人离开家园，迁往往往远在千里之外的省份。战争摧毁了中国无法用金钱估量的文化和社会价值。可能有150万中国人死于战争。其中约三分之一是无辜平民。

国家的财政损失目前也无法评估。然而，其程度可以从以下事实中推测：仅在闸北，受损或被没收财产的价值据信就超过战前货币10亿美元。中国只有两个主要城市幸免于难——北平和天津（尽管后者发生了一些激烈的战斗）。其他一些城市，如广州、南昌、长沙、汉口、苏州和徐州，则被日本的轰炸以及撤退的中国军队经常引发的火灾所摧毁。在这片广袤的土地上，几乎没有一个城镇能幸免于日本空袭者的轰炸，他们随意投掷炸弹，毫不顾及目标。

损失较小

日本的损失要小得多，因为战争是在中国土地上进行的。然而，即使是这些损失也是日本历史上最大的。一个非常保守的估计是，在中国阵亡的日本穿制服人员为25万人，受伤人数是其三倍。一船又一船包裹着白布、装满骨灰的小木盒正离开中国港口前往日本，在那里等待着哭泣的母亲、妻子和孩子。

就金钱而言，“中国事变”已使日本政府花费了近120亿日元，大约是整场日俄战争费用的七倍。此外，还有巨大的损失，形式包括失去出口市场、放弃和平工业、失业、资本转向非生产性行业、农业和海洋产量减少、产品质量下降、消费严重缩减以及日本硬通货储备耗尽。

还有一些无形的损失，例如，由于适龄男性被动员，1938年出生率下降了40%。

但最重要的是，日本的政治和经济结构发生了剧烈变化，从相对的自由主义和自由放任转变为并不亚于德国或意大利的严格军事管制。内阁已批准的人力及资本征用，是军方支持的走向军事法西斯主义的一系列漫长举措中的最新一步。

中国人决心坚定

当两年前战争爆发时，日本预计能快速战胜组织不善的北方部队，并随之加强对华北经济和政治结构的控制。中国迫切希望避免战争，但决心遏制灾难性的“吞并”进程，日本陆军正通过这一进程迅速啃食进入该国腹地。

pages.en:
Unfortunately for Nippon the
conflict spread to Shanghai and
what was expected to be an "in-
cident" became a major war. To-
day, the Japanese are as anxious to
have peace as the Chinese are
determined to fight until all the
territory lost since 1931 is recovered.
It is this gap which makes pro-
spects of peace very remote. Under
no conceivable circumstances—
except perhaps a major defeat in a
war with Russia—will Japan give
up the gains she had made in China
at the cost of thousands of lives.
Nor will she allow the functioning
of an independent Chinese Govern-
ment, which would ignore, for in-
stance, such major questions as the
supply of Chinese cotton for
Japanese textile mills.
The task the Japanese Army has
set before itself now is the re-
establishment of peace in the
"occupied areas," to make possible
their economic exploitation, which,
in turn, would recompense some of
the costs of war to Japan.
Peace, however, does not seem
possible as long as guerillas con-
tinue to harry Japanese garrisons,
block Japanese economic projects
and prevent the inflow of Nippon-
made goods. To root out guerillas,
the Japanese Fighting Services are
resorting to aerial terrorism, which
swells guerilla ranks by thousands
of new homeless and bitter men.
The re-establishment of peace is
closely allied with economic re-
covery. The latter is impossible as
long as the Japanese cling to their
present policy of strangling foreign
and Chinese enterprise and bleed-
ing the country white of its re-
sources.
The current stalemate will con-
tinue until the Japanese make a
costly and dangerous thrust into
"Free China," or until the Russo-
Japanese border friction bursts into
the flames of a major war. China
will be unable to break the dead-
lock until she acquires offensive
weapons—artillery, tanks, aircraft
—which she now lacks and which
she is not likely to secure in ade-
quate quantities in the near future.

Sharp Thrusts Continued

China's strategy for the time
being must rely on incessant sharp
thrusts at the outer rim of the
Japanese-occupied area and
simultaneous military and political
operations by the guerillas. In
this mode of warfare, as much
attention must be paid to armed
struggle as to the bolstering of
morale in the invaded territory
and to the blocking of Japanese
economic projects.
Thus far, the Chinese have been
relatively successful in these re-
spects. For instance, the output of
cotton in North China which the
Japanese need for their textile mills
has been reduced by 40 per cent,
mainly as the result of guerilla
agitation in favor of good crops.
Public morale has also been kept at
a high level, especially in North
China, where the Eighth Route
Army has formed the backbone of
Chinese resistance.
The Sino-Japanese war has thus
been converted into a contest be-
tween Chinese determination and
Japanese resources. If the Nippon-
ese Army can break China's morale,
it will rapidly consolidate its gains
in many parts of the country. If
Japan's resources are exhausted in
the near future, she will find her-
self compelled to seek the end of
war here by some means or other.
pages.zh:
对日本而言不幸的是，冲突蔓延至上海，原本预期只是一场“事变”，却演变成了一场大规模战争。如今，日本人渴望和平的心情，与中国人决心战斗直至收复自1931年以来所有失地的意志同样强烈。正是这种差距使得和平前景极为渺茫。在任何可以设想的情况下——除非在与俄罗斯的战争中遭受重大失败——日本都不会放弃她以数千条生命为代价在中国取得的成果。她也不会允许一个独立的中国政府运作，因为这样的政府会忽视诸如为中国纺织厂供应中国棉花等重大问题。

日军目前为自己设定的任务是在“占领区”重建和平，以便进行经济剥削，从而补偿日本的部分战争成本。然而，只要游击队继续骚扰日本驻军、阻碍日本的经济项目并阻止日货流入，和平似乎就不可能实现。为了根除游击队，日本战斗部队正诉诸空中恐怖主义，这导致成千上万无家可归且充满怨恨的人加入游击队行列。和平的重建与经济复苏密切相关。只要日本坚持其扼杀外国和中国企业、榨干国家资源的现行政策，经济复苏就不可能实现。

目前的僵局将持续下去，直到日本向“自由中国”发动代价高昂且危险的进攻，或者直到日俄边境摩擦爆发为大规模战争。中国无法打破这一僵局，直到她获得目前缺乏且在近期不太可能获得充足数量的进攻性武器——火炮、坦克、飞机。

持续猛烈突击

中国目前的战略必须依靠对日军占领区外围边缘进行不间断的猛烈突击，同时由游击队开展军事和政治行动。在这种作战模式中，必须像重视武装斗争一样，重视在被占领土上提振士气以及阻断日本的经济项目。

迄今为止，中国在这些方面取得了相对的成功。例如，华北地区供日本纺织厂所需的棉花产量减少了40%，这主要是由于游击队煽动支持丰收作物所致。公众士气也保持在高水平，特别是在华北，那里八路军构成了中国抵抗的中坚力量。

因此，中日战争已转化为中国决心与日本资源之间的较量。如果日军能摧毁中国的士气，它将迅速巩固其在全国许多地区的战果。如果日本的资源在不久的将来耗尽，她将发现自己被迫以某种方式寻求在此结束战争。
